His identifiable portfolio included national-security and nuclear-risk policy, support for Ukraine, federal policing accountability, industrial policy, climate investment, and veterans’ benefits. He converted several priorities into concrete action: the 2022 strategic reviews and Nuclear Posture Review, large-scale presidential security assistance, Executive Order 14074, the CHIPS and Science Act implementation launch, the Inflation Reduction Act’s administrative architecture, and initial PACT Act implementation (E002, E004, E007, E012, E013, E014). Independent records also show real execution weaknesses: Ukraine oversight had limited assurance and difficult weapons tracking, veterans’ mental-health integration and partnership monitoring remained incomplete, and the fiscal record included a large student-loan cost and a larger-than-projected deficit (E020, E034, E037, E047). Some actions demonstrated adjustment or institutional correction, but durable cross-domain outcomes were not yet observable. These are proven policy and oversight facts; broader claims about competence remain partly uncertain because Congress, states, agencies, partners, shocks, and inherited systems shared causation. The moral worth of the programs did not affect the execution score. The score exceeds the mixed-competence anchor because attributable implementation spanned several major priorities, but remains below 7 because independent durable results and adaptation are This supports low-to-moderate confidence and a broad range around a mixed score.","material_biases":[{"bias":"Conflict visibility and attribution bias","interpretation_effect":"Eastern-security reporting makes severe failures and crisis exposure highly visible, but cannot cleanly separate Tshisekedi’s decisions from armed-group action, regional actors, inherited insecurity, and external shocks.","likely_direction":"harms_ruler","supporting_evidence_ids":["E004","E033","E038"]},{"bias":"Donor and official implementation bias","interpretation_effect":"World Bank, IMF, presidential, and UN records document programs and formal actions more readily than independent durable outcomes; donor-supported outputs were therefore credited only as shared implementation.","likely_direction":"favors_ruler","supporting_evidence_ids":["E014","E021","E043","E053","E054"]},{"bias":"Opacity and suppressed-reporting risk","interpretation_effect":"Conflict access, state-of-siege restrictions, elite opacity, and incomplete domestic records may understate failures and distort denominators; silence was not treated as favorable evidence.","likely_direction":"uncertain","supporting_evidence_ids":["E036","E038","E055"]}],"no_blanket_regime_correction":true,"remaining_uncertainty":"FARDC command responsibility, durable ceasefire compliance, nationwide implementation, budget execution, electoral readiness, and correction after failures remain unresolved.","report_volume_not_used_as_severity":true},"calibrated_against":["dossier:2022-bias-contrast-v1:2022:USA:15810"],"calibration_batch_id":"chapter-judge:2022-bias-contrast-judge-v2:2022:8B","chapter_id":"8B","chapter_rationale":"Félix Tshisekedi’s 2022 record supports a mixed competence appraisal: 5.0/10. His identifiable portfolio combined security and regime-preservation goals with diplomatic conflict management, macroeconomic reform, education expansion, digital governance, judicial reform, and electoral preparation. He exercised formal presidential authority and translated several priorities into action: participation in Nairobi and Luanda peace processes, macroeconomic reforms, a national cybersecurity strategy, judicial appointments, an electoral calendar, donor-backed education and governance programs, and a ceasefire timetable (E002, E011, E014, E022, E035, E043, E053). Implementation was real but uneven. Free-primary-schooling reform remained unfinished, budget execution showed discrepancies, beneficial-ownership transparency was incomplete, and the state-of-siege period coincided with increased civilian deaths, democratic-space violations, and massive displacement (E004, E036, E038, E042, E054, E055). These outcomes are documented, but personal and causal attribution is often shared with armed groups, regional actors, donors, provinces, inherited administrative weakness, and shocks. Diplomatic coordination shows mobilization and crisis management, yet durable security progress and systematic adaptation are not demonstrated. The moral character of the programs did not affect the execution score. The score is above severe operational failure because Tshisekedi repeatedly converted priorities into institutions and processes, but below 6 because major objectives remained fragile and cross-domain
